case.title: An infrared flare in the galaxy NGC 3239 in 2020 that no optical survey saw: an obscured transient
case.hook: Found blind by Oddsky's mid-infrared difference imaging of 318 nearby galaxies (hunt H-0012): a flare peaking in 2020 November at about 5e5 L_sun, with no optical alert. Hubble caught a faint point source 85 days after the peak that has since vanished, and JWST found cooling dust at the same spot in 2024.
case.summary: A mid-infrared flare in the irregular galaxy NGC 3239 (about 8-12 Mpc), peaking in 2020 November at roughly 5e5 L_sun from ~960 K dust, that no optical survey reported. Hubble caught a faint, fading point source 85 days after the peak, and JWST found cooling dust at the same spot in 2024. Probably a dust-obscured stellar merger or eruption; a buried low-energy supernova is possible. Found blind by Oddsky hunt H-0012.

claims.text: WISE (unWISE neo11 epochal coadds, difference imaging): flat from 2010 to 2020 May 2; on 2020 Nov 23 W1 +232 +- 8 and W2 +308 +- 20 uJy above the 2010-11 level; 91/119 uJy in 2021 Apr, 38/42 in 2021 Nov, ~27 in 2022 Apr. Position 156.29118 +17.16387 (Gaia-tied, ~0.25"). Positive in both visit seasons, so not an asteroid (hunts/H-0012/reviews/ngc3239-check-2026-11-01.md).
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: The transient's W1-W2 is 0.95 +- 0.08 (~960 K dust); a blackbody gives ~5.6e5 L_sun at 7.9 Mpc (1.6-2.4x more at the 10-12 Mpc of SN 2012A's host distance and CosmicFlows-4). The rise is unresolved (< 205 d), so the true peak may be higher.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: HST (2021 Feb 16): a point source at 156.291224 +17.163778, 0.37" from the WISE centroid, F606W 25.93 +- 0.06 and F814W 24.95 +- 0.06 AB, present in all four 2021 exposures; absent in 2022 (F606W > 27.1) and in every 2025 filter, with no residual cluster (M_V > -2.9). The chance of an unrelated vanishing source within 0.37" is ~0.2%.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: JWST (programme 3707, 2024 Apr-May): a new unresolved source 0.01" from the HST position, F335M 5.9 uJy and F300M 3.2-3.6 uJy, nothing in F150W (> 26.5 AB): ~580 K dust at ~3.6e4 L_sun. Spitzer 2008 shows nothing there (> 8 sigma below the 2024 source).
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: No optical detection: no TNS object or ZTF alert; ATLAS limits o ~20.4-21.7 around the event; the galaxy was in solar conjunction in 2020 August. VLASS < 0.36 mJy (2021 Nov); Chandra 2025 < 2.6e37 erg/s.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Not a buried normal supernova as it stands: the HST colour allows A_V <~ 2, while the faintness relative to WISE needs A_V 9-20, and an enshrouded Type II SN should be 30-100x brighter in the infrared at this phase. An obscured luminous red nova (stellar merger), an ILRT-like eruption (no progenitor seen), or a low-energy SN behind clumpy dust fit better. Not an AGN: 2.7 kpc from the centre of a galaxy with no nucleus.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Not reported (2026-11-01): TNS, Gaia alerts, CBAT, ATel (web search), SPIRITS, MIRONG, the literature; no publication on the JWST 3707 data at this position. ADS full-text check of the De et al. WISE transient papers still owed.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: A dust-obscured stellar eruption or merger (luminous red nova or ILRT-like event) in NGC 3239, peaking around 2020 November.
hypotheses.would_falsify: A JWST spectrum showing supernova signatures, or a late radio detection of a normal SN.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: A low-energy or heavily, clumpily obscured core-collapse supernova whose dust is now cooling.
hypotheses.would_falsify: A spectrum of the remnant without supernova features.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: A WISE, HST or JWST artifact, or an unrelated variable star.
hypotheses.would_falsify: Already falsified by three instruments at one position.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

args.reason: WISE, HST and JWST see the same unreported object at one position
